route_1_method: BtbN's build is a graph of shell stages under `scripts.d/`. Each stage
it applies to this target/variant/FFmpeg version). `generate.sh` walks that
graph from the entry stage `scripts.d/zz-final.sh` and builds every enabled
stage it reaches. A stage that emits an `ffbuild_configure` flag becomes a
component on the FFmpeg configure line; a stage that emits none is built
into the same prefix and linked, but is invisible to the configure line.
This pass reproduces that walk for TARGET=win64 VARIANT=lgpl ADDIN=8.1
(FFVER 801) at the builder commit recovered for the shipped build, and
reports the reached-and-enabled stages that emit no configure flag.
The scripts are PARSED, never sourced or executed.

The artefact that would prove it - the release tag - was pruned by BtbN. Recovered and recorded by RELEASE PIPELINE; see docs/release/evidence/ffmpeg-shared-candidate/component-pins-SHIPPED-BUILD.json on branch agent/ffmpeg-shared-prov.

route_2_method: Search the shipped binary's bytes for markers that only that component's
own code would emit: vendor banners, assert source-file names, format
strings, mangled C++ symbol names. This is the route that caught FFTW, via
Every marker used is recorded per component in `detection_markers` so the
probe is repeatable and so a gate has something concrete to test.
derivation.routes_disagree_policy: Where the two routes disagree, BOTH are recorded and neither overrides the other. See `limits`.

limits: NEITHER ROUTE IS COMPLETE. This file names what was found, not everything that is there.
Route 1 reports what the build scripts DECLARED at an inferred commit. It does
not observe the build container, and it cannot know what the linker kept: with
--gc-sections, LTO and stripping, an archive can be built into the prefix and
contribute nothing to the final image.
Route 1 is also only one level deep in the way that matters. BtbN declares
dependencies at STAGE level; sub-scripts inside a directory stage all declare
only `base`, so the grouping is the dependency information. Below that, five
scripts fetch git submodules recursively and the vendored code they pull is
named nowhere in the pins - see `level_3_vendored_dependencies`.
Route 2 cannot prove absence. Absence of a string is not absence of code: a
stripped C library with no diagnostics (serd, sord, zix, sratom) leaves no
marker even when fully linked, and a header-only dependency leaves none by
definition.
Route 2 also cannot prove presence on its own. ffmpeg.exe embeds its entire
configure line and FFmpeg's own help text, so substrings such as `libdrm`,
`openssl` and `vorbis` occur as TEXT about components rather than as code from
them. Every `present` verdict below rests on a marker that FFmpeg's own text
does not contain; the raw substring counts are kept beside it so the
distinction stays auditable.
Licence identifiers were read from the upstream licence file at the pinned
revision where one exists, which is a higher bar than the surrounding evidence
(the 58-component inventory is largely `classification_confidence: low`). It is
still an engineering reading of a licence file, not a legal determination.

headline_effect: The inventory headline - 58 components / 42 attribution-only / 16 with a
source obligation / 0 GPL-only - DOES NOT CHANGE, and that is a real result
rather than a null one. All 12 newly found components are attribution-only,
so the obligation count does not move.
What changes is the completeness claim underneath it. The transitive layer is
20 components, not 9; one of the 9 (xorg-macros) is linux-only and is not in
this build at all; and the two components that DO carry an obligation
(fftw3, libudfread) were already known before this pass.
Stated plainly: the method was blind, the blindness was real and is now
measured, and on this particular build it happened to hide nothing new that

components.gate_note: A GPL-family-name match on `mbedtls` must NOT fail a copyleft gate on its own. The grant is dual and the recipient elects; a gate that treats the GPL half as decisive would fail every build for a component that carries no copyleft obligation here.
notes: THE MOST IMPORTANT NEW ENTRY, and the one most likely to be misread.
Mbed TLS is offered under Apache-2.0 OR GPL-2.0-or-later - the recipient
chooses. Electing Apache-2.0 leaves attribution only. It is NOT a second
It is worth naming anyway for three reasons. It is a GPL-family option
sitting inside an LGPL binary, so an automated scan will surface it and
someone will have to answer for it. `mbedtls` is on FFmpeg configure's own
EXTERNAL_LIBRARY_VERSION3_LIST, so a reader who checks that list will
assume it cannot be here - the list governs `--enable-mbedtls` as FFmpeg's
TLS backend, which is not what happened; librist pulled it in. And the
election should be recorded deliberately rather than left implicit.
Route 2 is inconclusive: the single `mbedtls` hit is librist's own error
message naming the API it calls, which evidences the CALLER, not the
callee. Route 1 says the archive was built and librist links it for its
CSPRNG. Recorded as route-1-only rather than upgraded.

build scripts fetch git submodules recursively. Whatever those pull is

Route 2 found two of these independently, which is the clearest evidence in

sc_obligation_assessment_2026_08_14.verdict: The unresolved level-3 sets are a RECORD-completeness gap (unrecorded git-submodule pins), not a compliance gap. On the evidence available, none of them introduces a new or stronger obligation than what is already disclosed and published, so no source archive or notice is missing on their account. What is genuinely open is (a) capturing the pins, and (b) confirming which subprojects reach the shipped library - both of which need a meson/cmake reproduction and are out of scope for a static pass.
per_set: identified (graphengine WTFPL, ggml MIT, highway Apache-2.0): all attribution-only, recorded; no source obligation.

libplacebo submodules (nuklear, glad, jinja, markupsafe, Vulkan-Headers, fast_float): all attribution-family licences (MIT / BSD / Apache-2.0 / public-domain-equivalent). No LGPL/GPL member, so the unresolved 'which reach the compiled library' question can only change WHICH attribution applies, never whether a copyleft or source obligation arises.

mbedtls submodules (framework, tf-psa-crypto): tf-psa-crypto follows mbedtls's own dual Apache-2.0 OR GPL-2.0-or-later grant, so the obligation is unchanged. Concrete record action: capture the tf-psa-crypto submodule pin at the build revision so it exists in a project record.
openssl submodules: 3.x submodules are test/fuzz corpora, not shipped code, so no obligation is expected; unverified at the pin, recorded rather than assumed.
level 4+: not examined; bounded by effort, not evidence.
residual_actions: RELEASE PIPELINE / build repro: record the tf-psa-crypto submodule pin and, if a meson/cmake reproduction is ever run for libplacebo/openssl, capture which subprojects were used.
No notice or source publication is blocked by this item.
